dialogue: I know.

dialogue: > Is he really worth more to you than everything we built?

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: > This isn't about worth. The decision was mine.

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: How disappointing. I dressed for an examination.

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: I assumed you'd prefer to remain conscious.

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: You're developing a suspicious familiarity with my preferences.

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: Occupational hazard.

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: You moved my appointment twice.

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: Scheduling difficulties.

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: And yet our schedules aligned so beautifully.

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: Perhaps fate is less inefficient than I thought.

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: I suspect fate has access to your calendar.

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: Do you resent being invited?

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: Not at all. I simply prefer to know whether I'm attending an appointment or participating in an experiment.

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: Why assume those are mutually exclusive?

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: And what would you be measuring?

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: That depends on what you're willing to reveal.

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: I might surprise you.

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: I would enjoy that.

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: Tell me something, Ilse.

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: Yes?

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: Do you ever meet anyone you don't want to understand?

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: Occasionally.

speaker: JEAN-PAUL
dialogue: And what do you do then?

speaker: VARGA
dialogue: I usually invite them back.

speaker: NEWS PRESENTER
dialogue: A dramatic split between two of the tournament's biggest stars, with Steffan Thomas reportedly at the center of the controversy!

speaker: REN
dialogue: That's not a fair representation of what happened.

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: No. It isn't.

speaker: REN
dialogue: Do you know who released it?

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: Not yet.

speaker: PUBLICIST
dialogue: Lyra, we can arrange an exclusive interview. Your followers are demanding a response.

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: My followers can wait.

speaker: PUBLICIST
dialogue: It would help manage the story.

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: I'm not interested in managing a story somebody else stole from me.

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: And cancel the interview with Steffan.

speaker: PUBLICIST
dialogue: But you're both scheduled—

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: Then he'll have an opportunity to practice talking without me.

speaker: REN
dialogue: You handled that well.

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: I wanted to throw the screen through a wall.

speaker: REN
dialogue: That might have been less effective.

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: You think?

speaker: REN
dialogue: The wall probably belongs to WAR.

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: Ren, I adore you.

speaker: REN
dialogue: Thank you?

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: Well, that's going to sell tickets.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: It was a private conversation.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: And now it's a very public conversation.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: You don't seem curious about who leaked it.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: Should I be?

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: Probably.

speaker: IBRAHIM
dialogue: May I have this dance?

speaker: COSSETTE
dialogue: If you remember who taught you.

speaker: COSSETTE
dialogue: Was that deliberate?

speaker: IBRAHIM
dialogue: I was hoping you wouldn't ask.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You're late.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Two minutes.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I was beginning to think you'd escaped.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: From dinner?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: It's a perfectly reasonable response to the food here.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You found somewhere that doesn't serve commemorative coffee.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I have many talents.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You don't talk much about your family.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: There's not much left to say.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You don't have to say anything.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: My sibling believed in WAR more than I did.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Really?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: They thought the company would bring opportunities to the colonies. Jobs. Infrastructure. A future.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I used to tease them for being so optimistic.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: And then?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: When the emergency happened, they kept saying the ships would come. That somebody would authorize them.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: They were right about the ships. The ships existed.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: They just didn't come.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'm sorry.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Sometimes I think if I can prove what happened, something will finally make sense.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Maybe it will.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: But you should get to have a life while you're doing it.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That's something you sound very certain about.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I have a lot of opinions.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I've noticed.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I spent most of my twenties moving from one contract to another. Repair bills, treatment bills, emergency jobs.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: And now you're here.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Now I'm trying to make enough money that I can stop pretending everything is temporary.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Which probably sounds terribly romantic.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: It sounds like you care about your mother.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I do.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You've become rather difficult to make fun of.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That sounds serious.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: It is. I may need professional help.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I've wanted to kiss you since the gala.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You have excellent timing. It only took you a week to mention it.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Is this the part where you charge me for your company?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: No. This one's on me.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I wasn't expecting to feel this close to anyone here.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Neither was I.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: > You know we're both still in the tournament.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: > I know.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: > And this may become complicated.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I'd still like to find out where this goes.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Good. So would I.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You're important to me. But I don't want to start a romance I may not be ready for.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I appreciate you telling me plainly.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Well.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Well?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I was going to say something clever.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: What happened?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You distracted me.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You know we're both still in the tournament.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I know.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: And I'm not going easy on you if we meet.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I wouldn't ask you to.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Good.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Coming in? We can talk, or we can call it a night. Really.

speaker: HALDANE (RECORDING)
dialogue: Ari Solano. Your qualifying performance has drawn the attention of our research division.

speaker: INSTITUTIONAL LIAISON
dialogue: Participating pilots may request meetings with relevant WAR departments through the research office. Access to unrelated corporate records is not guaranteed.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: Eight qualifiers remain! Here is the bracket!

speaker: ALEX
dialogue: This is where tournament ambitions meet complicated friendships.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: Every matchup was determined by a fight result and the published ranking rule. None of those relationships should decide who wins.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Well. Of course it's us.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I wish we had more time before this.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: So do I. But I need the prize money, Ari, and I need a real fight.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You'll get one.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Good. Then we're still on the same side, even when we aren't.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Ren for you, Crystal for me. Are you disappointed?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Only that you got the legendary champion before I could ask for a rematch.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Win tomorrow. Maybe we still get our own semifinal.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: No holding back if we do.

speaker: ALEX
dialogue: Hold on. Crystal is first even though Ari just beat her?

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: One win each in a closed three-way circle. The provisional announced seed breaks the standings tie. It doesn't reverse any fight result.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I can accept the rule and still wish it worked differently.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You can. And you can decide whether you want to talk about it before we fight.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I'd rather talk about us.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Then start with this: I am going to fight you properly.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: CRYSTAL DEVROE AND SELENE VALE ADVANCE FROM GROUP A!

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I wish you were in the bracket.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I do, too. But I'm not going to pretend I earned a spot.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Then what will you do?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Christian has a second copy of the Ganymede hold order. I can help make sure it survives the tournament.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I want to hear what you find. And I want you to know I'll fight Selene for myself.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I wouldn't ask for anything else.

speaker: ALEX
dialogue: Mara Voss defeats Ren Akiyama to win Group B!

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: Steffan Thomas takes Group C after a hard-fought victory over Lyra Kisaragi!

speaker: ALEX
dialogue: And Angel defeats Dante Vey to secure Group D!

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Congratulations. You earned your place.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Careful. Keep being nice to me and people will talk.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Exceptional pilots are invited to participate in our next-generation neural synchronization program.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I wouldn't dream of it.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: No holding back.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: So do I.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Win your match. I have plans for the semifinal.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Fair enough. I'm out. But I haven't run out of things to investigate.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I have a copy of the Ganymede order you should see.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Well, this is awkward.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: We knew it was possible.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Sure. So is being struck by lightning. I don't usually schedule breakfast around it.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You don't have to pretend you're happy about this.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'm not happy about it. But I'm going to fight you.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I know.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Seriously, Ari.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I need the prize money. And I didn't get this far by asking people to let me win.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I would never ask you to.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Good. Because if you go easy on me, I'll be furious.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: And if I win?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'll probably be furious for a little while anyway.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I like you. Quite a lot, actually.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That sounds serious.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Terrifying, isn't it?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: But I'm not going to pretend the rest of my life disappears because I met someone I like.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I wouldn't want you to.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Then we're all right.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: For now.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: For now.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You get Ren. I get the woman who won the championship before either of us had learned to drive.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You're looking forward to it.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Of course. When else do you get to hit a national monument?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Crystal's a better fighter than most people realize.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: So am I.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Don't get distracted by Ren's shiny technology.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I'll try.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Good. I'd hate to reach the semifinal and discover you weren't there.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That sounds almost romantic.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Don't spread it around.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'm facing Selene.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: She beat me. She can beat you too. Watch her counter on the left.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Advice, not pity. Good.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: What's that?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: An offer from the research division.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: What sort of offer?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Advanced neural synchronization. Experimental pilot assistance.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You're not seriously considering it.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I haven't decided.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Ari.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I know what you think of WAR.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: This isn't about what I think of their advertising.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: They're asking to put experimental hardware between your brain and your machine. You don't even know what it does.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That's why there's a consultation.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: A consultation run by the people selling it.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Just promise you'll find out what you're agreeing to.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I will.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Ari Solano. Congratulations on qualifying.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You invited me because I qualified?

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: We invited you because of how you qualified.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Your responses under pressure are unusually adaptable. But every conventional neural interface introduces latency between intention, machine interpretation, and movement.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: And yours doesn't?

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Ours reduces it. Sometimes substantially.

speaker: REN
dialogue: The difference can be remarkable.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You've been using it?

speaker: REN
dialogue: Voluntarily. For several months.

speaker: REN
dialogue: Some techniques that used to require constant conscious correction now feel natural.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: And the risks?

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Sensory distortions, temporary disorientation, altered motor awareness, and possible problems distinguishing assisted actions from self-initiated ones.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That last part sounds rather important.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: It is. That's why we're studying it.

speaker: REN
dialogue: I think the benefits are worth investigating.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I'm sure WAR does too.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: You have no obligation to participate. Your position in the tournament is unaffected by your decision.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: The invitation mentioned institutional contacts.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: We can arrange meetings with relevant departments. We cannot promise access to confidential records unrelated to the study.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: So the information about Ganymede isn't part of the deal.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: There is no deal concerning Ganymede.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: There is a research opportunity. You may accept it or decline it.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That's impossible.

speaker: REN
dialogue: Not impossible. It predicted the movement.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: And if the prediction is wrong?

speaker: REN
dialogue: The pilot can override it.

speaker: TEST PILOT
dialogue: I didn't tell it to finish that.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Predictive continuation. We're tuning the cancellation threshold.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: It ignored the pilot?

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Not exactly. It initiated a predicted response before the cancellation signal could be processed.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That sounds like a distinction that matters much more to you than to the person in the cockpit.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I understand why people want the enhancement. It makes ordinary controls feel slow.

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: And?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Twice I saw a machine start moving before the pilot expected it.

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: What did the pilot say?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That the system had anticipated the movement.

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: Did the pilot actually choose it?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That's what I'd like to know.

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: If you notice another one, capture the external diagnostic channel. Don't rely entirely on the central logs.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: The interface will begin with low-amplitude predictive assistance. You retain manual cancellation authority.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: And this recording isn't connected to WAR's servers?

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: Physically isolated.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: We have no objection to independent safety documentation.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That's... impressive.

speaker: REN
dialogue: It is, isn't it?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I barely had to think.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Your nervous system is adapting.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Wait.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: What happened?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I hadn't decided to move that way.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: The system may have anticipated the motor command before conscious awareness.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I understand the explanation.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I still want to know whether it was my decision.

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: Interesting.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: In a good way?

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: In the sense that I want another recording.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I could get used to this.

speaker: REN
dialogue: That's part of what makes it exciting.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Stop the simulation.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: What are you experiencing?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: The machine's hand. I can still feel it.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Transient body-schema persistence. Previously observed in some subjects.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: How long does it last?

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: Usually very briefly. We'll monitor you.

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: The report says you authorized the adjustment.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I didn't.

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: Are you certain?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: That's what bothers me.

speaker: PLUG
dialogue: The most expensive part of your machine now has a cheap scar.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: It suits the pilot.

speaker: PLUG
dialogue: The pilot is a walking invoice.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: So? Did they convince you to let them rebuild your brain?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: No.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Good.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You sound relieved.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I am relieved.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: It's impressive technology. Ren's almost impossibly fast with it.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'm sure.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: And I might be facing Ren tomorrow.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I know.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I might be giving up an advantage.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Maybe. But you don't have to accept every risk just because someone else does.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: If you change your mind, make sure it's because you understand the technology. Not because WAR made you afraid of losing.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You signed up.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: For a limited trial.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I asked you to be careful.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I was careful. I required independent monitoring.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: And did it work?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Very well. Until it made a movement I didn't expect.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Ari.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I stopped the test.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Good. Then stop the program.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I want to understand what happened first.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You can understand something without letting it keep experimenting on you.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You were in there for hours.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I wanted to see what the system could do.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: And?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I still feel the robot's fingers.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: That's not funny.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I wasn't joking.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Then why are you still considering the program?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Because it works. Because it might help me win. And because I might learn something about WAR that I can't find from outside.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You're talking about them like they're the only door in the building.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Maybe they're the only door I can get through.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Or maybe they've made sure you think that.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'm not telling you what to do.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: It feels like you are.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Then I'll say it differently.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'm frightened of what they might do to you. And I don't trust them to tell you when something goes wrong.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: We have enough to worry about without borrowing trouble from tomorrow.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Tomorrow's already here.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Then let's make it a good fight.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Then let's both make it through tomorrow.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Tomorrow we might have to fight each other.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Can we schedule being enemies for after breakfast?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You think you can distract me?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I think you still have my jacket.

speaker: ALEX
dialogue: An established champion against one of the tournament's most technologically ambitious newcomers!

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: Ren's timing has been extraordinary. But Crystal has faced every generation of HAR technology since the original championship.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: CRYSTAL DEVROE ADVANCES!

speaker: REN
dialogue: I was already changing the command when it attacked.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: Then why did it attack?

speaker: REN
dialogue: That's what I intend to find out.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: I'd like to know too.

speaker: REN
dialogue: I'm looking forward to this.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You're remarkably cheerful about trying to knock me out of the tournament.

speaker: REN
dialogue: It's an opportunity to test two different approaches to piloting.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: And to win.

speaker: REN
dialogue: That too.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: Your fighting style is unusual.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: That's a polite way of saying my equipment is held together with optimism.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: And excellent timing.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Don't compliment me until I've beaten you.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Three copies of the same Ganymede order. Three different approval timestamps.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Somebody passed it through three departments and called that independent authorization.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: That's one possibility. What can we actually verify?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I came here believing a trophy would make everyone listen. I don't have one. I still have this.

speaker: ALEX
dialogue: Ari Solano against Mara Voss. Two of the tournament's most surprising competitors.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: And two pilots who have spent a considerable amount of time training together.

speaker: ALEX
dialogue: Which must make this difficult.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: It also means neither can afford to underestimate the other.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: How are you feeling?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Like I'm about to fight someone who knows all my best tricks.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You taught them to me.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: An error in judgment, clearly.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Ari, whatever happens—

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I know.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: No. Let me finish.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I don't want you deciding what I need more than I do.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I won't.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: And if you win, don't look at me like you've done something terrible.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: What if you win?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Then you can buy me dinner.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Ready?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: As I'll ever be.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Good. No holding back.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: No holding back.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: ARI SOLANO ADVANCES TO THE SEMIFINALS!

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Mara—

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You won.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I know.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: You fought well.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I hate that.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I really needed this.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: I know.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: No. You know part of it.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'm happy for you. I will be. Just not entirely right now.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: What do you need?

speaker: MARA
dialogue: A little time.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: And don't you dare apologize for fighting properly.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: MARA VOSS ADVANCES!

speaker: ARI
dialogue: You got me.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I did.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Fair and square.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Are you all right?

speaker: ARI
dialogue: My pride may need treatment.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: I'll add it to the medical bills.

speaker: MARA
dialogue: Thank you for taking me seriously.

speaker: ARI
dialogue: Always.

speaker: ALEX
dialogue: We have been anticipating this match all week!

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: So have the fighters, although I suspect their reasons differ from ours.

speaker: DANTE
dialogue: You wanted this.

speaker: STEFFAN
dialogue: More than you know.

speaker: DANTE
dialogue: Then enjoy it while you can.

speaker: STEFFAN
dialogue: You always were generous with threats.

speaker: DANTE
dialogue: And you always talked too much.

speaker: STEFFAN
dialogue: Then make me listen.

speaker: STEFFAN
dialogue: That was a good fight.

speaker: DANTE
dialogue: Don't.

speaker: STEFFAN
dialogue: Dante—

speaker: DANTE
dialogue: You got what you wanted. Go celebrate.

dialogue: The advanced-systems annex wants emergency renewal of its research authorization. It says the sunset clauses are obsolete.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Then its engineers can explain why the old clauses still exist.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: You've signed waivers before.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Power isn't the problem. It's who gets to exercise it.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: You've been looking at our procurement presentations all evening.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: And you've been counting who watches them.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: An occupational hazard.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: Yours or theirs?

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: Don't mistake curiosity for a vote. Or a date.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: I won't. Though I suspect you make both rather difficult to earn.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: Only for people accustomed to buying them.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: Someone treated your vote as a permanent license.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: That's not what I authorized.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: The public may not distinguish the two.

speaker: IBRAHIM
dialogue: If it can climb the arena wall, it can also clear the spectator barrier.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: And it won't. Precision is a form of restraint.

speaker: COSSETTE
dialogue: An unusual slogan for a board meeting.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: One pilot owns the public's attention. The other would like to own the network carrying it!

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: I'd have asked for a better metaphor.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: The model assumed she'd commit to the opening.

speaker: COSSETTE
dialogue: She changed her mind. People do that.

speaker: LYRA
dialogue: Well played. Now don't tell anyone I should take a board seat.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: You'd be terrifyingly good at resigning.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: An absence is not evidence of a conspiracy.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: Then don't call it one. Call it an unfilled control and ask who accepted the risk.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: They'll say the engineers assured them.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: You used to find that reassuring.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Your endorsement would make people listen.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: To me, or to your logo behind my shoulder?

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: I want that commission to survive a board vote.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: Then write it so it survives without my face.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: What would you do if you weren't someone's heir?

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Probably find a smaller company to disappoint.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: That's almost an honest answer.

speaker: STEFFAN
dialogue: You spend so much time chairing meetings. Are you sure you remember which button makes it fight?

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: It's the one you keep pressing when someone says Dante's name.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: They'd decline jurisdiction.

speaker: STEFFAN
dialogue: You might try sounding less satisfied with yourself.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: Your campaign team has already drafted a statement.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Tell them to keep the adjectives. I'm not leaving the station.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: No procurement press release until after this next fight.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: You don't have to prove your competence in a cockpit.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: For once, I'd like the result to be mine alone.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: No independent observer can evaluate what our current integration systems do. We agreed on oversight suitable for the previous generation.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Then you needed a new authorization.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: We needed time. You never built a board that rewarded truth delivered on schedule.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: You appear wherever I find a weak control.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: Then you should be more concerned about your controls.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: I don't date companies.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: I'm trying to become more interesting than one.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: If we subpoena ourselves, the board will call you reckless.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: If we don't, someone will call us what we are.

speaker: SORELL
dialogue: You want to halt the announcement three days before our largest public event in a decade.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: I want to halt a test until we can explain it.

speaker: HALDANE
dialogue: There is no approved body with the necessary expertise. Your hold will create risk, not reduce it.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Then we'll appoint one that isn't managed by your department.

speaker: SORELL
dialogue: If you damage the company, you'll answer to this board.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: That's the only sentence today I agree with.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: What did our experts think they were preserving?

speaker: REN
dialogue: At first, a person. They also preserved a technology they wanted.

speaker: ANGEL
dialogue: Both can be true. So can the lack of consent in what followed.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: You can call this a merger of interests.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: I would rather call it two people comparing notes.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: If I find that you've used what I told you as leverage against me, this ends.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Then I will put the provenance in writing.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: Your motion has votes if you promise the directors you won't turn over internal correspondence.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: An inquiry with that promise is a press release.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: A press release might still win you the chair.

speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogue: The command log credits Kreissack.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: He's not on the biological control channel.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Then someone saved these people and forged the signature.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: You're learning. It's expensive.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: You finally did something that may cost you your seat.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: I'm not sure that means it was noble.

speaker: SELENE
dialogue: No. But it's a more interesting answer than your speeches.

speaker: SHIRRO
dialogue: And let the record show—no committee can vote away what happened in that arena!

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: You are not authorized to expand this system.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: You'd call that freedom?

speaker: NOVA
dialogue: You called your agreements safeguards. Some were decorations.

speaker: KREISSACK
dialogue: Apparently, I can still surprise you.

speaker: SORELL
dialogue: You've chosen a poor moment to surrender influence.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Influence was how we got here.

speaker: SORELL
dialogue: And what replaces it? Your conscience?

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: An external body with the right to tell us no. Even when it costs us.

speaker: MIRA
dialogue: You could lose the seat.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: I may finally find out what I was worth without it.

speaker: POLITICAL COMPROMISE
dialogue: He appears on a press dais, surrounded by allies. The reforms are real but bounded, and investigators are still requesting the unreleased records. Sorell applauds with an unreadable expression.

speaker: DARK CONSOLIDATION
dialogue: A private executive elevator rises to the highest office. Milano has attained authority, but the empty observation seat behind him is a visual reminder that competence without supervision can become another version of Kreissack's certainty.

speaker: MILANO
dialogue: Nor should it be.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I'm not a family member of a trophy.

speaker: CURATOR
dialogue: We have a separate registry for former competitors.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Good. Use that one.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: You never come to these things for the speeches.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Neither do you.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: Mine pay for the catering.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Then they can afford to tell the truth on the placards.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: I don't want a quotation. I wanted to know whether that panel was as dishonest as it looked.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Which part?

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: The full historical record has been restored.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: They are missing a shipping signature. That's a question, not a scandal.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: You're more cautious than your reputation.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: My reputation is a secondhand story told by people who never asked me anything.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: For the record, that was not an invitation to become a source.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: For the record, I wasn't going to.

speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogue: You want the truth or the whole file?

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: The part I'm entitled to examine without turning innocent people into exhibits.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: You'll hear more about the tournament than this. I'm sorry.

speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogue: I work on missing records. I know how that goes.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: You can feel whatever you feel when he looks at you. I won't pretend I don't see it.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: Then don't pretend that makes it your decision.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I'm afraid you'll let him explain away facts before we find them.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: And I'm afraid you'll call every choice I make a mistake until it belongs to you.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I don't know how to do this without trying to take charge.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: Then you can learn. I'm having to.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: We've proved someone lied about where the record went. We have not proved how the ship died.

speaker: NEUTRAL RECORDS OFFICER
dialogue: That's still worth writing down.

speaker: OFFICER
dialogue: He could say the designation was legitimate.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Then we compare it with the licensing authority that should have issued it.

speaker: OFFICER
dialogue: No such license exists.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: That's the conclusion I want in your words, not mine.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: You were right about the record.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I was suspicious. Now there is proof of the hold. Those are different things.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: You didn't say "I told you so.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: It's taking everything I've got.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: Your sister's body language is not evidence. And your grief is not a credential. I'm going to ask whether the archive lied, not whether you're sympathetic.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I should be relieved.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: You look offended.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I'm not used to someone refusing my best arguments.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: Then you haven't listened to your sister lately.

speaker: BROKER
dialogue: You don't have to like him. You just have to choose the bigger crime.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: There isn't a bigger crime discount. Give your information to the independent examiner.

speaker: BROKER
dialogue: You want justice or a clean conscience?

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I want evidence that survives somebody asking how I got it.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: So the blackout caused the collision?

speaker: ENGINEER
dialogue: No. The flight-control command caused the fatal deviation. We can show the blackout existed, and that it removed an emergency channel. We cannot show the crew would otherwise have survived.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Then put that in the final report. Exactly that.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: If you keep seeing Raven, people will call the evidence a lovers' quarrel.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: They'll call it that if I never speak to him again. They don't get to decide whether I want him. You don't either.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I thought I was keeping you safe.

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: You were trying to make the future predictable.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Isn't that what an investigation is?

speaker: CRYSTAL
dialogue: An investigation asks what happened. It doesn't get to choose what happens next.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: You found a thing no one can cross-examine.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Give it ten minutes.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I'd rather not make my parents the reason you said yes.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: Good. Because they aren't.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Their words reached someone. Not nowhere. Someone.

speaker: ARENA MARSHAL
dialogue: We need an extra pair of hands by the family exit.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: You have them.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Check your equipment. Call me when you're clear.

speaker: PRODUCER
dialogue: Tell us what she can't see.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: I can tell you what the documents say. Her feelings aren't your property.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: We can make the story simpler if we say the machine was responsible all along.

speaker: COSSETTE
dialogue: We can also make it false.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: Then I don't want it simpler.

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: We found the man who ordered it. Too late to ask him anything.

speaker: OFFICER
dialogue: Not too late to establish the record.

speaker: COUNSEL
dialogue: In your opinion, did Raven murder your parents?

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: My opinion isn't why I'm here. What I can establish is that he authorized a blackout, saw a request to restore the channel, refused, and hid the evidence afterward. A separate attack caused the fatal deviation. The independently authenticated authorization names Kreissack as the

speaker: CHRISTIAN
dialogue: We tried that once. It lasted eleven minutes.

speaker: LEENA
dialogue: Twelve. You spent the first minute pretending you didn't see me.
